title: Mooren’s Ulcer: The Peripheral Storm
summary: Mooren’s ulcer is a rare, idiopathic, and devastating form of peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK). Characterized by severe pain and a distinct overhanging leading edge, it remains a diagnosis of exclusion that requires aggressive multi-modal management to prevent corneal perforation.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Mooren’s ulcer is an idiopathic, progressive, necrotizing peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK) that begins at the limbus and extends circumferentially and then centrally. It is uniquely characterized by the absence of associated systemic autoimmune disease and the absence of scleritis. It typically presents with a 'furrow' appearance with an undermined, overhanging leading edge of deep-seated corneal melting.

rows: Younger patients (2nd-3rd decade), often African descent
Slow, responds well to medical therapy
Rapid, relentless, poor response to therapy

sections.title: Clinical Features & Symptoms
content: Severe Ocular Pain (disproportionate to signs)
Photophobia and Blepharospasm
Lacrimation and Redness
Blurred Vision (from induced astigmatism or axial involvement)
Circumferential spread of ulceration
Absence of Scleritis (CRITICAL differentiator)

content.explanation: M: Marginal location; O: Overhanging leading edge; O: Ocular pain (severe); R: Resistant to simple therapy; E: Exclusion of systemic disease; N: Non-sclerotic (Sclera is spared).

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Peripheral stromal thinning (furrowing) starting at the limbus.
Undermined, 'overhanging' leading edge of the ulcer.
Vascularization of the ulcer base (neo-vascularization follows the melt).
Epithelial defect over the area of active melting.
Spared central 'island' of cornea in early/moderate stages.
Total conjunctivalization in end-stage disease (conjunctival flap effect).
Descemetocele or perforation in aggressive Type 2 cases.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup (Exclusion Protocol)
content: Step 1: Clinical History (Rule out recent surgery, trauma, or chemical injury).
Step 2: Rule out Systemic Autoimmune Disease (RF, ANA, c-ANCA, p-ANCA, ESR, CRP).
Step 3: Rule out Infectious Keratitis (Corneal scrapings for Gram stain, culture, and PCR for HSV/VZV).
Step 4: Serology for Hepatitis C (Highly associated) and HIV.
Step 5: Physical Exam (Focus on joints, skin, and respiratory system to exclude GPA or RA).
Step 6: Confirm diagnosis of Mooren's if all systemic/infectious tests are negative.

rows: Clear space between limbus and infiltrate, blepharitis
Ring infiltrate, history of contact lens use

sections.title: Management Algorithm (Step-Ladder)
content: Level 1: Intensive Topical Steroids (Prednisolone Acetate 1% q1h) + Prophylactic Antibiotics.
Level 2: Topical Cyclosporine A (0.05% - 2%) or Tacrolimus ointment.
Level 3: Conjunctival Resection (Peritomy) - 3mm back from the limbus adjacent to the ulcer.
Level 4: Systemic Immunosuppression (Oral Prednisolone 1mg/kg + Methotrexate or Azathioprine).
Level 5: Biological Agents (Infliximab or Rituximab) for refractory Type 2 cases.
Level 6: Surgical Repair (Tectonic AMT, Lamellar Keratoplasty, or Cyanocrylate Glue).

sections.title: Surgical Techniques & Interventions
content: Conjunctival Recession/Excision: Removes the source of collagenases and inflammatory mediators.
Amniotic Membrane Transplantation (AMT): Multi-layered for tectonic support and anti-inflammatory properties.
Lamellar Keratoplasty (Crescentic): Used for structural integrity after the inflammatory phase is controlled.
Glue and BCL: Emergency management for micro-perforations (<2mm).

sections.title: Complications & Prognosis
content: Corneal Perforation & Endophthalmitis
Secondary Glaucoma (Peripheral anterior synechiae)
Cataract formation (Steroid-induced or inflammatory)
High Irregular Astigmatism
Phthisis Bulbi in severe, untreated Type 2 cases

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Resident
content: Always look for 'The Lip': The overhanging edge is pathognomonic.
If there is scleritis, it is NOT Mooren's. Look for GPA or RA.
Check Hepatitis C status in every Mooren's patient; treatment of HCV can help resolve the ulcer.
Early systemic immunosuppression is mandatory for bilateral disease.
Mooren's is a diagnosis of exclusion—biopsy only if an infection is suspected.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Evidence
sections.content: Recent studies have highlighted the efficacy of Rituximab (anti-CD20) in severe, refractory cases of Mooren's Ulcer, suggesting a significant role for B-cell mediated pathology. Additionally, the use of topical Medroxyprogesterone has been explored to inhibit collagenase activity in the melting leading edge.
